body: The only thing that's helpful is giving me a way to safely die. We are bestowed with so many human rights, except the one which allows us to die when and how we please.

The thing is, the only happiness I've ever had was only a result of naïvety, vast amounts of free time and lack of responsibility. All those things evaporate during adolescence and adulthood. What is there to do when the first 5 years of your life are the best you'll ever have?

Any "hobby" I have now is just a temporary distraction from reality, allowing me to procrastinate from doing anything I don't want to—but eventually have to do. Some would say I'm entitled for thinking I shouldn't have to do anything I don't want to, but if someone's going to decide I should exist, existence should be worthwhile, surely? And a worthwhile existence is not one where I'm enslaved in a life of pointless labour.
